newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurers, police combat car accidents.
newsitem.headline: German insurers, police combat car accidents.

text.p: Germany's insurers are seeking closer cooperation with the police authorities in the prevention of car accidents.
With a new computer programme introduced on Wednesday, the police will in future be able to evaluate accidents electronically and identify frequent accident spots.

"If you don't know what happened when and where, you cannot prevent it," said Dr Volker Meewes, head of the loss prevention unit of the German insurance federation Gesamtverband der Deuschen Versicherungswirtschaft (GDV).
GDV paid for the development of the electronic accident map, (Elektronische Unfalltypen-Steckkarte EUSka) and the work was undertaken jointly with the police.

"The programme can save time and increase police presence," Thomas Kuehl, police chief in Dreseden, where EUSka has been tested, said, adding that there was now a much higher quality of data from the accidents.

The system replaces manual maps, where coloured needles indicate types of accidents. "The programme enables us to identify circumstances that push up accident figures, so we can react faster," Kuehl said.

Police use laptop computers to gather all information while at the accident site. The programme checks the input for plausibility. The location of the accident can be marked precisely on a digital map.
The German police will now test EUSka in three states.
"Eventually, the programme will be made available to all police forces free of charge," said Meewes.
